title: optimize quant kernels: int8/fp8 smoothquant + dequant-fusion + kvcache-aware batching
author: Aisha Rahman
description: This PR implements a set of coordinated runtime optimizations for quantized inference kernels focused on INT8 and FP8 paths and smoothquant/dequant fusion. Motivation: customer workloads show regressing tail latency and increased token cost for quantized model variants when KV cache hits are frequent and sequence lengths vary. The changes target three areas: 1) kernel-level fusion to fold dequantize+gemm into a single kernel for INT8/FP8 paths where hardware supports mixed-int math, reducing memory bandwidth and extra temporaries; 2) smoothquant-aware scaling support that avoids redundant per-token re-scaling when KV cache prefixes are reused across requests; 3) scheduler and batching improvements that make continuous-batching KV-cache-aware so requests with large cached prefixes are routed into low-latency fast-path batches while cold-starts are batched for throughput. The PR includes microbenchmarks showing 20-35% lower p99 latency on typical chat workloads and 12-18% token-cost reduction due to fewer dequant/reshard copies. Backwards-compatible feature flags are provided to roll out changes and compare perf in canary pools.
commits: 3 commits: 1) kernel: add fused dequant+gemm kernel and FP8 INT8 bridges, 2) runtime: add smoothquant scaling cache and KV-cache hit fast-path hooks, 3) scheduler: kvcache-aware batching policy + unit tests and perf benchmarks
